FEATURE.NAME: active
FEATURE.GLOSS: The Actor/Senser/Sayer is the grammatical Subject. The process unfolds from the participant. (e.g., "K-Electric reduced supply.")

FEATURE.NAME: passive
FEATURE.GLOSS: The Goal/Phenomenon is the grammatical Subject. The Agent is backgrounded or deleted. (e.g., "Supply was reduced [by K-Electric].")

FEATURE.NAME: material
FEATURE.GLOSS: Processes of doing and happening in the external world. Construes change in the physical or social environment. Participants: Actor, Goal. (e.g., "K-Electric reduced supply.")

FEATURE.NAME: mental
FEATURE.GLOSS: Processes of sensing — thinking, feeling, perceiving, desiring. Requires a conscious Senser. Participants: Senser, Phenomenon. (e.g., "People know the situation.")

FEATURE.NAME: relational
FEATURE.GLOSS: Processes of being, having, and becoming. Classifies or identifies entities. Participants vary by sub-type: Carrier+Attribute (attributive) or Token+Value (identifying). (e.g., "Power is a basic necessity.")

FEATURE.NAME: verbal
FEATURE.GLOSS: Processes of saying and symbolic exchange. Boundary process between mental and relational. Participants: Sayer, Receiver, Verbiage, Target. (e.g., "K-Electric claims a shortage of oil.")

FEATURE.NAME: behavioral
FEATURE.GLOSS: Processes of physiological and psychological behavior. Boundary between material and mental. Participants: Behaver, Behavior. (e.g., "People suffer in the heat.")

FEATURE.NAME: existential
FEATURE.GLOSS: Processes asserting the existence of entities. Typically realized by there is/are. Participant: Existent. (e.g., "There are repeated technical faults.")

FEATURE.NAME: creative
FEATURE.GLOSS: Brings something into existence that did not exist before. Verbs: build, create, make, write, compose, develop, produce. Example: "K-Electric produces energy."

FEATURE.NAME: transformative
FEATURE.GLOSS: Changes or transforms an already-existing entity. Verbs: reduce, increase, improve, fix, damage, destroy, alter. Example: "The pandemic reduced consumption."

FEATURE.NAME: transitive
FEATURE.GLOSS: Action directed at and affecting a Goal. Verbs: hit, break, take, unleash, hold, deliver, use. Example: "K-Electric unleashed load-shedding on the people."

FEATURE.NAME: intransitive
FEATURE.GLOSS: Action or event with no Goal. Only Actor is present. Verbs: run, walk, go, come, sit, last, happen. Example: "People go in their state of misery."

FEATURE.NAME: ditransitive
FEATURE.GLOSS: Action involving both a Goal and a Beneficiary (Recipient or Client). Verbs: give, send, deliver, offer, provide. Example: "They deliver energy to consumers."

FEATURE.NAME: cognition
FEATURE.GLOSS: Processes of thinking, knowing, understanding, believing. Verbs: know, think, believe, understand, consider, realize. Example: "Both governments must take notice of this situation."

FEATURE.NAME: perception
FEATURE.GLOSS: Processes of sensory or evaluative perception. Verbs: see, hear, feel, notice, observe, seem, appear. Example: "It seems even more senseless this time around."

FEATURE.NAME: reaction
FEATURE.GLOSS: Processes of emotional reaction, feeling, or attitude. Verbs: like, hate, fear, enjoy, find (evaluative), mind. Example: "Relatives find it much more difficult."

FEATURE.NAME: desideration
FEATURE.GLOSS: Processes of desire, intention, or wish. Verbs: want, wish, hope, desire, intend, need. Example: "The people need uninterrupted power supply."

FEATURE.NAME: attributive
FEATURE.GLOSS: Assigns a quality or characteristic to a Carrier. Structure: Carrier + Attribute. NOT reversible. Verbs: is, are, was, become, remain, seem, appear. Example: "The heat becomes unbearable." (Carrier=heat; Attribute=unbearable)

FEATURE.NAME: identifying
FEATURE.GLOSS: Defines or identifies one entity in terms of another. Structure: Token + Value. IS reversible (Token=Value and Value=Token). Verbs: is, represents, equals, means, defines, constitutes. Example: "Power is a basic necessity." (Token=Power; Value=basic necessity)

FEATURE.NAME: circumstantial
FEATURE.GLOSS: Locates a Carrier in a circumstantial relation. Structure: Carrier + Circumstantial Attribute (at/in/on a location or time). Example: "Karachi is in the grip of long power outages."

FEATURE.NAME: possessive
FEATURE.GLOSS: Indicates ownership or possession between entities. Structure: Possessor + Possessed. Verbs: have, own, possess, contain, include. Example: "The company has thousands of employees."

FEATURE.NAME: addressee-oriented
FEATURE.GLOSS: Saying directed at a specific Receiver/addressee. Verbs: tell, inform, ask, order, promise, instruct. Example: "K-Electric often tells the public about oil shortage."

FEATURE.NAME: non-addressee-oriented
FEATURE.GLOSS: General acts of communication not directed at a specific addressee. Verbs: say, state, announce, claim, report, mention. Example: "One reason K-Electric uses for this is the shortage of oil."

FEATURE.NAME: physiological
FEATURE.GLOSS: Bodily actions reflecting physical states or biological processes. Verbs: breathe, cough, sleep, sweat, endure, suffer. Example: "People endure long power failures."

FEATURE.NAME: psychological
FEATURE.GLOSS: Observable behaviors reflecting mental or emotional states. Verbs: smile, laugh, stare, cry, worry, frown. Example: "People worry about the situation."

FEATURE.NAME: verbal-behavioral
FEATURE.GLOSS: Behavioral processes that overlap with verbal processes — communicative behaviors. Verbs: chat, grumble, murmur, complain, mutter. Example: "Residents grumble about the outages."

FEATURE.NAME: neutral
FEATURE.GLOSS: Asserts the simple existence of an entity. Realized by there is/are/was/were. Example: "There are also repeated technical faults at Bin Qasim Station."

FEATURE.NAME: eventive
FEATURE.GLOSS: Asserts the occurrence of an event or happening. Realized by there occur/happen/exist. Example: "There happen to be faults at the station."

FEATURE.NAME: actor
FEATURE.GLOSS: Entity that performs, initiates, or causes the material process. In active clauses = Subject. In passive = Agent (by-phrase). Example: "K-Electric [Actor] unleashed load-shedding."

FEATURE.NAME: goal
FEATURE.GLOSS: Entity that is directly affected, impacted, or brought about by the material process. In passive = Subject. Example: "K-Electric unleashed load-shedding [Goal]."

FEATURE.NAME: beneficiary
FEATURE.GLOSS: Entity that benefits from the action. Realized as indirect object or prepositional phrase (to/for). Example: "They deliver energy to consumers [Beneficiary]."

FEATURE.NAME: range
FEATURE.GLOSS: Specifies the domain, scope, or extent of the process without being affected by it. Closely tied to the process verb. Example: "She plays the piano [Range]."

FEATURE.NAME: client
FEATURE.GLOSS: Entity for whose benefit the action is performed, when not identical to Recipient. Often realized by for-phrase. Example: "She baked a cake for him [Client]."

FEATURE.NAME: senser
FEATURE.GLOSS: The conscious being who perceives, thinks, feels, or desires. Must be human or personified entity. In active = Subject. Example: "Both infected people and relatives [Senser] find it difficult."

FEATURE.NAME: phenomenon
FEATURE.GLOSS: What is perceived, thought about, felt, or desired by the Senser. Can be a Thing, Fact, or Act. Example: "People know the situation [Phenomenon]."

FEATURE.NAME: carrier
FEATURE.GLOSS: Entity that bears or is assigned an Attribute (in attributive clauses). Typically the Subject. Example: "The heat [Carrier] becomes unbearable."

FEATURE.NAME: attribute
FEATURE.GLOSS: Quality, characteristic, or class assigned to the Carrier (in attributive clauses). Typically Complement. Example: "The heat becomes unbearable [Attribute]."

FEATURE.NAME: token
FEATURE.GLOSS: The sign or expression being defined/identified (in identifying clauses). The variable element. Example: "Power [Token] is a basic necessity."

FEATURE.NAME: value
FEATURE.GLOSS: The meaning, identity, or definition assigned (in identifying clauses). The constant element. Example: "Power is a basic necessity [Value]."

FEATURE.NAME: possessor
FEATURE.GLOSS: The entity that owns or possesses something (in possessive clauses). Example: "The company [Possessor] has thousands of employees."

FEATURE.NAME: possessed
FEATURE.GLOSS: The entity that is owned or possessed (in possessive clauses). Example: "The company has thousands of employees [Possessed]."

FEATURE.NAME: sayer
FEATURE.GLOSS: The entity that produces the verbal act. Need not be human — reports, signs, documents can be Sayers. Example: "K-Electric [Sayer] claims a shortage of oil."

FEATURE.NAME: receiver
FEATURE.GLOSS: The entity to whom the verbal act is addressed. Only present in addressee-oriented verbal processes. Example: "K-Electric told the people [Receiver] about the shortage."

FEATURE.NAME: verbiage
FEATURE.GLOSS: The content of the verbal act — what is said. Can be a direct quote, indirect report, or nominalization. Example: "K-Electric claimed [Verbiage: a shortage of oil]."

FEATURE.NAME: target
FEATURE.GLOSS: The entity at which the verbal act is directed (in verbal acts like criticize, accuse, blame). Example: "The editorial accuses K-Electric [Target]."

FEATURE.NAME: behaver
FEATURE.GLOSS: The conscious entity exhibiting the behavioral process. Analogous to Senser in mental processes. Example: "People [Behaver] endure long power failures."

FEATURE.NAME: behavior
FEATURE.GLOSS: The behavioral act itself (optional participant). Analogous to Range in material processes. Example: "She [Behaver] gave a sigh [Behavior]."

FEATURE.NAME: existent
FEATURE.GLOSS: The entity whose existence is asserted. Follows the existential process verb (there is/are). Example: "There are repeated technical faults [Existent] at Bin Qasim Station."

FEATURE.NAME: location
FEATURE.GLOSS: Specifies where or when the process takes place.

FEATURE.NAME: extent
FEATURE.GLOSS: Specifies the distance or duration of the process.

FEATURE.NAME: manner
FEATURE.GLOSS: Specifies how the process takes place — quality, means, or comparison.

FEATURE.NAME: cause
FEATURE.GLOSS: Specifies why the process takes place — reason, purpose, or behalf.

FEATURE.NAME: contingency
FEATURE.GLOSS: Specifies a conditional or concessive relationship to the process.

FEATURE.NAME: accompaniment
FEATURE.GLOSS: Specifies what or who accompanies the process.

FEATURE.NAME: role
FEATURE.GLOSS: Specifies in what guise or capacity an entity participates.

FEATURE.NAME: matter
FEATURE.GLOSS: Specifies what the process is about or concerning. Probe: about what? with respect to what? Example: "of this situation"

FEATURE.NAME: angle
FEATURE.GLOSS: Specifies the viewpoint or source from which the process is seen. Probe: from whose viewpoint? according to whom?

FEATURE.NAME: spatial
FEATURE.GLOSS: Answers: Where? Realized by prepositional phrases of place. Prepositions: in, at, on, near, across, through, over, under. Example: "across the city" / "at Bin Qasim Station"

FEATURE.NAME: temporal
FEATURE.GLOSS: Answers: When? Realized by prepositional phrases or adverbs of time. Prepositions: in, at, on, during, after, before, recently. Example: "in summer months" / "this time around"

FEATURE.NAME: spatial-extent
FEATURE.GLOSS: Answers: How far? The distance covered by the process. Example: "for miles" / "throughout the country"

FEATURE.NAME: temporal-extent
FEATURE.GLOSS: Answers: How long? The duration of the process. Example: "for as long as 12 hours" / "throughout the summer"

FEATURE.NAME: means
FEATURE.GLOSS: Answers: By what means? Specifies the instrument or method of the process. Example: "either because of planned load-shedding or due to technical faults"

FEATURE.NAME: quality
FEATURE.GLOSS: Answers: How? In what manner? Realized by adverbs of manner. Example: "substantially" / "immediately" / "seriously"

FEATURE.NAME: comparison
FEATURE.GLOSS: Answers: Like what? Realized by comparative phrases. Example: "as they normally would have" / "like most megacities"

FEATURE.NAME: reason
FEATURE.GLOSS: Answers: Why? The cause or motivation for the process. Prepositions/conjunctions: because, because of, due to, owing to, since. Example: "because of the fact that households are at home"

FEATURE.NAME: purpose
FEATURE.GLOSS: Answers: For what purpose? The intended goal of the process. Prepositions: for, in order to, so as to. Example: "for this practice" / "to take care of the patient"

FEATURE.NAME: behalf
FEATURE.GLOSS: Answers: For whose sake? On whose behalf is the process carried out? Prepositions: for, on behalf of. Example: "for the residents of Karachi"

FEATURE.NAME: condition
FEATURE.GLOSS: Answers: Under what condition? A conditional dependency on the process. Conjunctions: if, unless, provided that, in case. Example: "If the supply of furnace oil is inconsistent..."

FEATURE.NAME: concession
FEATURE.GLOSS: Answers: Despite what? An unexpected or contrasting condition. Conjunctions: though, although, even though, despite. Example: "Though the practice has become a routine matter..."

FEATURE.NAME: comitative
FEATURE.GLOSS: Answers: Together with whom/what? An entity accompanying the process. Prepositions: with, together with, along with. Example: "with millions of apartments in close proximity"

FEATURE.NAME: additive
FEATURE.GLOSS: Answers: In addition to what? An entity added to the process. Prepositions/adverbs: also, as well, in addition, at the same time. Example: "at the same time" / "also"

FEATURE.NAME: guise
FEATURE.GLOSS: Answers: As what? In what capacity? Specifies the role in which an entity participates. Prepositions: as, in the role of. Example: "as a pretext to power outages"

FEATURE.NAME: product
FEATURE.GLOSS: Answers: Into what? What the participant becomes as a result of the process. Prepositions: into, as. Example: "turned into a crisis" / "privatized as a company"
